🇲🇽🛢️ MEXICAN CRUDE DROPS 5.15% TO $77.75 AS HORMUZ REOPENS — SHEINBAUM SAYS LOWER PRICES SHIELD FUEL SUBSIDIES

Mexican mezcla crude fell 5.15% to $77.75/barrel today — its lowest since March — after Trump and Iran reached a peace framework set for formal signing in Switzerland Friday. WTI dropped to $80.75 (-4.87%), Brent to $83.35 (-4.56%). The peso held firm near 17.20/dollar, on its 7th straight session of gains.

Sheinbaum at her mañanera: oil around $80 (down from over $110 during the war) actually helps Mexico's public finances because the government subsidizes gasoline and diesel via the IEPS — every dollar cheaper means less fiscal cost. Iran's resistance broke the blockade, the Strait of Hormuz reopens, and Mexican drivers come out ahead.

Source: El Financiero

🚨🇲🇽 TRUMP ORDERS DOJ TO INVESTIGATE GAVIN NEWSOM — FEDERAL AGENTS RAID HOMES OF EX-COLLABORATORS WITH NO CRIME ALLEGED

California Gov. Gavin Newsom says Trump has ordered the Department of Justice to investigate him and his wife. Federal agents have visited the homes of his former associates seeking records — without any specific allegation of illegal conduct.

Newsom: 'They have not found a crime — they are simply trying to find one.' His read: this is retaliation for criticizing Trump and a possible 2028 presidential run. The US is now openly weaponizing its DOJ against domestic political opponents — the exact 'lawfare' playbook Washington has spent decades exporting to Latin America against Lula, Correa, Cristina, Evo, AMLO.

Source: Regeneración

🔥🇲🇽 'QRGATE' — PRI'S 500-PESO VOTE-BUYING SCHEME EXPOSED IN COAHUILA, WITH POLICE COVER AND DRONE TRUCKS

PRI ran a digital vote-buying operation in 16 Coahuila districts paying ~500 pesos per ballot — coordinated through a QR-code data platform, with local police protecting the buyers and a drone-equipped truck stationed outside Morena offices to intimidate party leaders.

Morena's response: complaints filed with the Federal Electoral Tribunal, INE, and Financial Intelligence Unit. National president Ariadna Montiel: 'We will pursue investigations at all levels.' Same playbook as Peña Nieto's 2012 Monex/Soriana scheme — but now tracked digitally and shielded by uniformed officers.

Source: Contralínea

🇲🇽📚 INEA: 958 MIGRANT FARMWORKERS GET FREE BASIC EDUCATION — STUDY FROM ANY STATE

Mexico's National Institute for Adult Education (INEA) now guarantees free literacy, primary, and secondary schooling to 958 migrant agricultural workers — accessible from any state via the AprendeINEA platform, on phone, tablet or computer. Workers take certification exams wherever harvest brings them.

INEA Director Armando Contreras Castillo: 'The educational scheme aims to ensure that agricultural workers can start, continue, and finish their studies regardless of which state they are in.' For the first time, residency is decoupled from the right to education. The system bends to the worker, not the other way around.

Source: Contralínea

🚨🇲🇽 SHEINBAUM TO US DOJ: NO EVIDENCE, NO ROCHA HANDOVER — SOVEREIGNTY ENFORCED

The US Department of Justice requested urgent detention of Sinaloa Gov. Rubén Rocha Moya and 9 other Mexicans for extradition — without delivering any evidence. Today Sheinbaum told them: deliver proof or the request gets rejected.

'If the United States does not deliver the evidence, that urgent detention request can be rejected, independent of the investigation by the Attorney General's Office.' There is no deadline forcing Mexico to act. Context: the US has rejected 36 Mexican extradition requests for 'lack of evidence.' Mexico is applying the same standard back.

Source: La Jornada

🚨🇲🇽 HOMICIDES DOWN 46% UNDER SHEINBAUM — MAY 2026 IS THE LOWEST MAY SINCE 2015

Daily homicides fell from 86.9 (Sept 2024) to 47.3 (May 2026) — a 46% drop in 20 months. Over 56,000 detentions for high-impact crimes, nearly 30,000 firearms seized, 420 tons of drugs recovered (including 5 million fentanyl pills), and 2,407 clandestine labs dismantled.

The strategy: intelligence, coordination, address root causes. No mass incarceration, no Bukele theater, no US 'war on drugs' recipe. Sheinbaum: 'I want to publicly recognize the security cabinet — my gratitude, my admiration for the work they do.'

Source: La Jornada

June 15, 2026 | 🔴

📰 An ambush near Nahuatzen, Michoacán, gets folded into the larger narrative: Mexican authorities "have confirmed the attack" but "little has been done to capture the gunmen." The implication — Sheinbaum's sovereignty stance is why cops keep dying.

The article ties this to her "resistance to U.S. pressure on cartel eradication and her protection of cartel-linked politicians."

🔴 What's missing: the Sig Sauers and Glocks the cartels are using were trafficked south from Arizona dealers. The same week, Center for International Policy documented the supply chain. Breitbart doesn't mention guns. The blame stays one-directional.

REUTERS/AOL: Trump on USMCA: "We don't need anything Mexico has"
June 16, 2026 | 🤡

📰 As US-Mexico negotiators sit down for round two on agriculture and energy, Trump tells reporters: "I'm not looking to renew it… We don't need anything that Canada has. We don't need anything that Mexico has, but they need everything that we have."

The framing repeats the line as a quirky Trump moment. The reality: $1.6 trillion annual regional trade. Mexico is the US's #1 trading partner. The "we don't need them" line erases who actually grows the tomatoes, who actually assembles the cars, who is actually the largest US export market.

🔴 The article notes "analysts suggest his remarks may be a negotiating tactic." No Mexican voices in the piece pushing back.
